name: Resume after change approval (awaiting_approval → executing)
description:
The dev loop SHALL NOT start until a human approves the generated change. This rule is the release side of the first human gate: a run parked in awaiting_approval returns to executing only once run.change.decision == "approve" is present, at which point dev_from_task becomes eligible for the run's tasks. Without an approve decision the run stays parked — the gate holds. Rule-owned transition (G2). CONTRACT: the approval adapter MUST stamp run.change.decision on the RUN entity (subject = agent.run.entity-id), or the run never resumes.

SINGLE-VALUED DECISION (nl-conversation-intent D13, group 8) — this rule and the CANCEL rule (run-lifecycle/07) are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a partition each must remember to carry. They previously read two independent booleans (run.change.approved / run.change.rejected) and each guarded on the OTHER being absent, because the exact-command fast-paths could stamp one without reading the other and leave a run holding BOTH — a run that then fired NEITHER rule and was wedged at the gate permanently, with no park, no post, and no operator surface. That cell was documented as an accepted 'unsurfaced stall'; the external review was right that documenting a permanent wedge is not fixing it. One single-valued fact under replace-by-predicate makes the contradictory state UNREPRESENTABLE, so the guards are gone and the cell no longer exists.

on_enter.reason: human approved the change; resuming to develop from the approved tasks
